structure.title: Revolt and pursuit
structure.text: The poem opens after the heavenly conflict, then moves between Satan's enterprise, heaven, and Eden. Earlier events are told within that movement.

structure.title: Choice and consequence
structure.text: Conversations about freedom, obedience, and knowledge converge on the human pair's decisions and their aftermath.

people.name: Satan
people.text: The fallen archangel who wakes in Hell after losing a war in Heaven, and rallies his followers with some of the finest speeches in the poem.

people.name: Adam and Eve
people.text: The first man and woman, living in Eden with one rule to keep, still learning what their love, their work and their freedom are.

people.name: Raphael
people.text: An archangel God sends to Eden to warn Adam of his enemy, who stays to dinner and tells the history of the war in Heaven.

context.title: Genesis expanded
context.text: Milton enlarges a brief biblical account into conversations, motives, and cosmic history. His imaginative additions are part of his interpretation.
context.takeaway: Distinguish biblical outline from poetic invention.

context.title: Epic speeches
context.text: Leaders persuade listeners by presenting danger, honour, and necessity in particular ways. A magnificent speech can conceal a poor argument.

notice.text: Compare freedom claimed with dependence displayed.
notice.why: Characters may describe themselves more generously than their actions warrant.
Ordinary affection and disagreement carry the cosmic argument into daily life.

opening: Satan has lost a war against God and immediately begins explaining why defeat need not count as defeat. His speeches make rebellion sound magnificent, even as revenge becomes his governing purpose. Meanwhile Adam and Eve inhabit a world they have not yet learned to distrust. Milton gives the catastrophe of the Fall the scale of an epic and the intimacy of a relationship: persuasion, pride, tenderness, and the terrible possibility of choosing something because the person you love has already chosen it.
